**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement imposes no exclusivity on Corio:

- **Sections 2.1–2.4, 2.2, 2.3, 12.3** — all licenses to Corio are expressly *nonexclusive*; nothing obliges Corio to source e-procurement software or marketplace services solely from Commerce One.
- **Section 2.7 (Restrictions)** — scope-of-use limits (no reverse engineering, no unauthorised copying), not sourcing restrictions.
- **Section 13 (Shared Resources)** — no restraint on Corio using third-party integrators or competing products; Section 13.6 expressly preserves each party's independent development rights.
- **Exhibit D (Sales and Marketing Cooperation)** — introduced as "non-binding" cooperation efforts; the cross-selling incentive, joint marketing and initial-customer items create no requirements commitment or preferred-provider status.
- Directional check: the only real restraints (Section 2.4 — Commerce One may not contact Corio Customers regarding non-ASP license sales and must refer inbound Customers to Corio) run **in our favour** and are correctly left untouched under the rule's guidance.

This satisfies the preferred position ("No exclusivity or 'sole supplier' obligation on Customer"), so nothing is redlined.
